title: IRRS Rule Set
description: Schema for one versioned IRRS rule-set file (standards/irrs/<semver>/rules.yaml, parsed as JSON before validation). The rule set is a product asset consumed by the Go scoring service and the Python assessment pipeline; it must never live inside a single service. Published (active) rule sets are immutable: fixes are made by creating a new version directory, never by editing files in place.

code.description: Internal Readiness Standard identifier. Only IRRS exists in the MVP.

version.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the rule set. Must match the directory name it is stored in.

status.description: draft: pending PO review, must not score production runs. active: published and immutable. retired: no longer used for new runs; historical runs keep their bound version.

dimension.description: IRRS dimension codes per PRD §11.1: D1 Discoverability, D2 Comprehensibility, D3 Decision Support, D4 Task Completion, D5 Payment Readiness, D6 Recovery & Help, D7 Cultural Context.

journey_stage.description: International visitor journey stages per PRD §5.1.

severity.description: S0 Blocker, S1 Critical, S2 Major, S3 Minor, Info suggestion (per PRD §11.2). Severity is never multiplied into scoring weights; S0/S1 findings are reported separately as blocking/critical issues.

evidence_type.description: Evidence types per PRD P0-2. A rule may only require types the ingestion pipeline supports; 'url' means either a registered source or a snapshot (capability decided per release).

code.description: Stable business identifier of the rule. Codes are unique within a rule-set version and are the key used by assessments, findings and eval cases. This is NOT the database primary key (runs bind standard_version_id + rule id); renaming a code is a breaking change and requires a new rule-set version.

description.description: What is checked, phrased so a reviewer can decide PASS/WARN/FAIL without guessing. Must be answerable strictly from the listed evidence; anything not observable in evidence must end in UNKNOWN, never a guess.

weight.description: Relative weight inside the dimension (dimension scores normalize by evaluated weight, so absolute size only matters relatively). 0 is legal for placeholder rules but such rules never influence scores.

evaluation_type.description: deterministic: decidable by code from evidence metadata. ai: model proposes the conclusion from evidence. hybrid: model proposes, human confirmation mandatory before the result counts as reviewed. human: model may only propose candidates; a human decision is required for any status (e.g. actual payment success).

review_required.description: When true, the finding does not count as reviewed until a human confirm/edit/na decision exists (PRD §15.3 lists payment, allergen, legal, accessibility topics).

min_count.description: Minimum number of matching evidence items. If fewer are bound to the run, the correct outcome is UNKNOWN/insufficient_evidence — never a guessed status.

must_show.description: Semantic markers the evidence must plausibly show (e.g. qr_landing_page, payment_signage). Used by deterministic candidate filtering and grounding checks; markers are free-form but stable within a rule-set version.

entity_types.description: Project entity types the rule applies to. Outside these the rule is N/A (excluded from the applicable set), not UNKNOWN (missing evidence) — the distinction is normative for scoring (ADR-0002).

target_locales.description: BCP-47 target visitor locales the rule applies to, or ["*"] for locale-independent rules. The target language decides the perspective of the check (can the target visitor read it?), not the report language.

rationale.description: Why this rule exists and why this severity/weight. This is the defense when the rule is challenged and the input for human severity/weight review.

status.description: Per-rule status inside the rule set. Only active rules are candidates for new runs; draft rules are carried in the file for review but must not be selected as applicable scoring items.
